Electromyography of all four limbs, including F-waves and somatosensory potentials, indicated a conduction block at the spinal level but produced inconclusive results. A: The image is an MRI T1-weighted view showing a long strip of lesions causing spinal cord compression in the cervical canal, consistent with spinal epidural abscess. B: T2-weighted MRI shows hyperintensity of the lesion within the spinal canal, consistent with inflammatory changes or epidural collection associated with spinal epidural abscess. C: T1-enhanced MRI showing annular enhancement and spinal cord compression, classic radiological signs of an epidural abscess. D: Axial T1-enhanced MRI shows a ring-enhancing lesion in the right posterior spinal canal, characteristic of a spinal epidural abscess. E: Coronal T1-enhanced image demonstrating a hypointense lesion in the spinal cord canal, contributing to the diagnosis of epidural infection. F: Coronal T1-enhanced image of soft tissue changes (honeycomb-like area) adjacent to the spinal canal, supporting the presence of an associated epidural/paravertebral collection.

(A,B) Sagittal planes of T1WI, T2WI, and T1W FS with gadolinium enhancement sequences demonstrate abnormal T2 hyperintense signal change at the C5-C6 intervertebral disc (white arrow) as well as associated destruction of C5-C6 endplates, representing spondylodiscitis. (C) Evidence of prevertebral abscess at the C5-C6 level (black arrowhead).

source_variant.figure_caption: Midsagittal T2-weighted MRI of the cervical spine The image demonstrates extensive C3-C4 spondylodiscitis with significant inflammatory changes. A large prevertebral abscess (red arrow) is visible, extending from C2 to C6 and causing anterior displacement of the retropharyngeal soft tissues. At the C3-C4 level, a critical anterior spinal epidural abscess (white arrow) is seen, leading to severe spinal cord compression with a residual spinal canal diameter of only 5 mm. A diffuse intramedullary T2 hypersignal is present from C3 to C6 (blue arrow), consistent with acute compressive myelopathy.
